Liberty Criminal Justice transfer plans: online and residential are different

Liberty’s online and residential Criminal Justice B.S. programs both total 120 credits, but their requirement lists and transfer guides differ. Our reviewed starting proposals assign 72 credits outside Liberty for online study and 74 for residential study. Choose the format you actually want before choosing courses.

The school name is only the beginning

A student searching “Does Liberty accept Sophia?” may find several useful university pages. The missing detail is which Liberty program and completion format the course will serve. A residential student needs the residential requirements and receiving equivalents, while an online student needs the online versions.

This comparison covers the general Criminal Justice B.S. in the 2026–27 catalog. A concentration or another degree can change the plan. Both starting proposals assume no completed student courses and show a supported mix of outside learning and Liberty coursework.

Your decision may include more than the course totals. Online study can fit work or family responsibilities. Residential study can provide the campus setting a student wants. Decide on that experience first, then use the appropriate course plan.

Two complete proposals, with different remaining work

The online proposal places 72 credits in selected outside options and 48 at Liberty. The residential proposal places 74 outside and 46 at Liberty. Both account for 120 credits, with each requirement counted once. These are proposed placements from reviewed course maps, not credits awarded to a particular student.

The two-credit difference is not evidence that the campus program is faster or cheaper overall. Campus housing, meals, travel, tuition arrangements, financial aid, prerequisite sequences, and actual course availability belong in that comparison. Forty-six campus credits also do not establish a one-year finish.

Compare the available degree plans

Look at the actual requirements that change

The online plan includes UNIV 104, Instructional Technology for Successful Online Learning, as a three-credit requirement. The residential plan instead includes UNIV 101, Foundational Skills, worth one credit. Those are different courses in different degree structures.

The religion and theology sequence also differs. The online proposal includes four-credit RLGN 104, BIBL 104, and THEO 104 requirements. The residential proposal uses its own two-credit course sequence, including RLGN 105, BIBL 105, BIBL 110, THEO 201, and THEO 202. A title that sounds similar should not be used to move a credit amount from one plan to the other.

The reviewed residential proposal also selects a Study.com option for INFT 110, Computer Concepts and Applications, and two specifically mapped one-credit elective options. Those details help explain why a finished plan needs individual rows rather than a blanket “transfer 90 credits” statement.

Some outside options appear in both routes

There are also shared examples. Both starting proposals select Sophia English Composition I for ENGL 101, Sophia Public Speaking for COMS 101, and Sophia Intro to Criminal Justice for CJUS 200. They select a Study.com option for CJUS 230 and another for CJUS 310.

Shared examples can make comparison easier, especially for a student who may change plans. They do not establish that every outside course works in both formats. Use the full requirement list to see where a selected course applies and whether another requirement or an elective slot is already filled.

Keep a single record of your original course, including provider, code, credits, unit system, and completion date. Compare that record against each route. Changing the destination should change its proposed placement, not the facts of what you earned.

Build the purchase sequence around the chosen route

Apply previous learning before buying new courses. Then group the remaining outside options by provider and course requirements. If a subscription gives access to several applicable classes, the amount completed during the paid period determines its realized cost.

Leave the selected Liberty coursework in view while planning the calendar. Major courses, prerequisite order, and school requirements can determine when the final work is offered. The overall transfer ceiling is a limit, not a substitute for the named outside matches in the degree plan.

For a campus student, also establish the experience you want to preserve. More transfer can reduce campus coursework, but someone who wants two years on campus may choose a different balance than someone prioritizing the shortest possible stay.

Open the correct plan and keep your courses

The two public plan pages below show the selected courses and remaining university requirements. Begin with the format that fits your life, then adapt it to your records and preferences. If you later compare another degree, your saved course collection stays available.

You do not need to prepare a new spreadsheet from scratch to explore the difference. Start with one supported route, inspect the rows that matter, and use the other proposal as a clear comparison.

About this research

DegreeSteps editorial team · Degree planning and transfer-credit research

We explain educational choices using university catalogs, receiving-school course agreements, provider guidance, and the same researched degree models used by DegreeSteps.
